subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The First American Financial Leak
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The First American Financial Leak.

hook.text: 885 million mortgage documents sat on a public website. Anyone who changed the URL could see them.

buildup.text: First American Financial, a title insurance giant, stored records online with sequential URL numbers.

discovery.text: By changing one number in the web address, anyone could access bank accounts, tax records, and SSNs.

twist.text: This wasn't a sophisticated hack. It was a design flaw so simple a child could exploit it.

climax.text: 885 million records exposed not by genius hackers, but by basic web design negligence.

punchline.text: Change one number in the URL. See someone's mortgage.

quiz.question: How were First American Financial records exposed?
options: A simple URL design flaw allowed access by changing a number
